Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Crane Yard

15 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 4.6 min

The load chart and the pick plan, plus programming the anti-collision zone the yard actually needs.

Critical Lift Plan & Signalperson

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.7 min

The lift where the plan and the signalperson are the load path: a chart read against its own limit, one voice running the pick, and the exclusion zone that keeps everyone else out from under it.

  • ASME — ASME B30.26 — Rigging hardware
  • ASME — ASME B30.5 — Mobile and locomotive cranes
  • ASME — ASME B30.9 — Slings
  • union — IUOE local training funds and the IUOE National Training Fund — operating and stationary engineer apprenticeship
  • NCCCO — NCCCO mobile crane, tower crane and rigger/signalperson certification
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1926.1425 — Keeping clear of the load (cranes and derricks in construction)

What it proves

Competency: Rig and land a load to an engineered lift plan

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 3 of its 6 stations, against ASME B30 Safety Standard for Cableways, Cranes, Derricks, Hoists, Hooks, Jacks and Slings; OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart CC Cranes and derricks in construction; NCCCO Certified Crane Operator programme; ETCP Entertainment Technician Certification Program — Certified Rigger.

These stations also count toward:

  • Crane and Rigging — the lift plan, the load and the landing (5 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: ASME B30 rigging and crane practice, NCCCO operator knowledge, and ETCP entertainment rigging for the theatre station. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
